correctness_risks.rationale: No serious bugs, but the promise-level caches turn a transient API failure into a permanent one, and there is no error boundary for non-404 failures — the spec explicitly says to treat the API as a live service.

readability.rationale: A new teammate would find their way quickly: consistent naming, one route per file matching the spec, comments where they matter; the untyped API payloads are the main rough spot.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:18-27 — cache-poisoning fix is a required change, not a nit
app/src/lib/data.ts — typed API interfaces for the heavily-used payloads would be requested
app/src/lib/components.tsx:95-97 — dead Missing() component to delete

review_cost.rationale: One round of real changes (cache resilience, error boundary, payload types) plus a handful of nits; nothing structural enough to block the PR.

findings.issue: Failed fetch promises are cached permanently, so a single transient API error makes that resource unavailable until the process restarts; same for the module-level species/version-group promises in data.ts:27-42.
findings.suggestion: Delete the cache entry when the promise rejects (catch-and-remove, or wrap so only successful resolutions are cached) and let 404 nulls remain cached.

findings.issue: No defaultErrorComponent / catch boundary; any non-404 API failure surfaces as the framework's default error screen.
findings.suggestion: Add a defaultErrorComponent (and optionally a route-level catchBoundary) that renders a friendly error page with a retry link.

findings.issue: Server-only code and shared types live in the same module; client files (app/src/lib/components.tsx:4, app/src/lib/MovesTable.tsx:3) import types from it, and the boundary is guarded only by convention — one dropped `import type` would bundle process.env and the fetch cache into the client.
findings.suggestion: Move CardData/MoveRow/EvoNode into a shared types module (or a format.ts-adjacent file) and add a 'server-only' import guard to pokeapi.ts/data.ts.

findings.issue: Unbounded Promise.all fan-out: a version group with ~200 moves fires 200 simultaneous requests; the same for 40 version groups at data.ts:45-47.
findings.suggestion: Add a small concurrency limiter (e.g. chunked batches of 8-16) — the local API tolerates it, but it's cheap insurance.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled anchor scrolling with rAF plus a 150ms setTimeout duplicate; the router has first-class support (scrollRestoration: true in createRouter).
findings.suggestion: Enable scrollRestoration in app/src/router.tsx and drop the effect.

findings.issue: API payloads are typed as any throughout the data layer, so the strict tsconfig protects almost nothing here.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the payloads actually consumed (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type, Generation) — they're few and stable.

findings.issue: Missing() component is dead code; routes import the MISSING string directly.
When ?page exceeds the total (e.g. ?page=99), the last page renders but the URL still claims page 99.
findings.suggestion: If currentPage !== page, replace the URL with the clamped page (or let validateSearch clamp it).

findings.issue: Only /data/ and /.data-cache/ are ignored; app/.output and app/.tanstack build artifacts are not, so the generated server bundle risks being committed.
No typecheck step (build is vite build only) and no app-level tests for the pure logic (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, sort ordering, idFromUrl).
findings.suggestion: Add a `typecheck` script running tsc and lightweight unit tests for format.ts/MovesTable ordering.

summary: This is a genuinely idiomatic TanStack Start codebase on the current stable release: correct use of createServerFn().validator(), loaderDeps, validateSearch, notFound() and the official nitro/vite toolchain, with clean route-per-page organisation and readable, commented code. The main merge blockers are resilience and hygiene: permanently cached rejected promises, no error boundary, an untyped data layer, and a convention-only server/client boundary in data.ts. I'd merge after one focused round of fixes.
